featured_reviews.name: Kavita Mahendra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Most arrogant doctor

I am giving 1 star as that’s the only option I wish I could rate in negative

We chose to consult Dr Punjabi based on the positive reviews online, but it turned out to be a serious mistake.

My aunt, who is 85 years old and a heart patient, went to see him with her previous medical reports—something any responsible patient would carry. Instead of reviewing them, he rudely snapped at her, saying, “Who asked you to show this report? I don’t want to see another doctor’s report.” This is not just unprofessional, it shows a complete disregard for basic medical protocol and patient care.

What was even more disturbing was his tone and attitude. He spoke so harshly to an elderly woman that she was left shaken, apologized to him, and came back home in tears. This is absolutely unacceptable. No patient—especially a senior citizen—should be treated with such arrogance and disrespect.

We later came to know of a similar incident where another elderly patient, who mistakenly came a day early for his appointment, was bluntly told to “Get out.” This clearly isn’t a one-off incident but a pattern of deeply insensitive and rude behavior.

A doctor’s job is not just to treat but to show empathy and basic human decency. Unfortunately, Dr Punjabi seems to have completely forgotten that. No level of qualification justifies this kind of behavior.

If you value dignity, respect, and humane treatment—especially for elderly family members—I would strongly advise you to think twice before consulting him.

I sincerely hope he reflects on his behavior and learns to treat patients with the dignity they deserve.

This has been one of the most disappointing medical experiences I’ve had. We visited this cardiologist for a second opinion, bringing along an angiography CD to assess the percentage of blockage and determine whether angioplasty was necessary or if medication could suffice.

Unfortunately, the doctor was unable to confidently read the CD. Initially, he said he wasn’t sure if there was any blockage at all (raising serious doubts about his expertise as a cardiologist). Then, within just 15 minutes, his diagnosis fluctuated from no blockage, to 30%, to 70%, and finally 70–80%. This inconsistency was alarming and did not inspire confidence.

He began the consultation by noting blood pressure, weight, and other basic vitals. While reviewing the case history and previously prescribed medications, he recommended discontinuing *Cortel-CH* (prescribed by another doctor), claiming it could cause headaches and flush sodium from the body. However, he soon became confused, tore up the initial prescription, and scribbled a new one—this time only listing *Ecosprin Gold-40*, with no other notes or patient details. When asked why he discarded the original, he said it was “messed up,” and that he remembered the measurements, which seemed unprofessional and careless.

Regarding treatment, he first stated that angioplasty wasn’t necessary, then suddenly reversed his stance and strongly recommended it—specifically at Holy Family Hospital in Bandra—while dismissing other reputable hospitals like ACE and Tunga without providing clear reasoning.

Lastly, the consultation fee was ₹4,000, which is fine if the expertise justifies it. But in this case, with so much confusion and lack of clarity, it felt unjustified.

I had chosen him based on reviews mentioning over 15 years of experience, but what we experienced did not reflect that. If you are looking for a reliable, knowledgeable, and confident cardiologist, I would strongly recommend seeking another opinion. Very disappointed with the overall experience.
